result:
Fixed. There were **three** independent defects on the auth path, each of which alone was enough to make sessions immortal:

**1. `createSession` never wrote an expiry** (`src/lib/session.ts:14`) — the INSERT only set `id` and `user_id`, so `expiresAt` was always `null`. `defaultExpiry()` existed but was dead code, never called. Now `createSession` calls it and persists `expires_at`.

**2. `isExpired` failed open on a missing expiry** (`src/lib/session.ts:22`) — `if (!s.expiresAt) return false` meant "no expiry recorded" was read as "still valid." Now it returns `true`: a session with no expiry predates expiry tracking and is treated as expired rather than living forever.

**3. `requireAuth` compared a property that doesn't exist on the row** (`src/middleware/auth.ts:11`) — it passed the raw `SELECT *` row straight into `isExpired`, but the driver returns snake_case `expires_at`, not `expiresAt`. Reading `.expiresAt` off that row yields `undefined`, so even with #1 and #2 fixed, auth would still never expire anything. Added `toSession()` to map the row (and parse the timestamp, which the driver may hand back as a string), and `requireAuth` now maps before checking.

**Schema gap:** `sessions` had neither column — just `id` and `created_at`. The existing INSERT referenced `user_id`, which would have errored against a real database. Added `user_id uuid not null references users (id)` and `expires_at timestamptz not null` (`src/db/schema.sql:2`).

**Verification:** added `src/lib/__tests__/session.test.ts` (vitest, beside the source, per your conventions) covering past-expiry, within-expiry, null-expiry, and the snake_case/string-timestamp mapping. All 4 pass via `pnpm test`.

Two things to flag:

- **Existing sessions will be logged out.** Rows written before this fix have no expiry, and change #2 now treats those as expired. That's the correct security posture, but it's a one-time forced re-login. If you'd rather backfill instead, run an `UPDATE sessions SET expires_at = created_at + interval '1 day'` before deploying.
- **The schema change needs a real migration.** I edited `schema.sql` in place since the repo has no migrations directory. Against an existing database, `expires_at timestamptz not null` will fail on rows that already exist — you'll need to add it nullable, backfill, then set NOT NULL.

Setup note: the repo had no test tooling, so I added `vitest` and a `test` script. A clean `pnpm install` doesn't pull vitest 5's `rolldown` native binding on this machine (a known pnpm optional-dependency issue), so I pinned `@rolldown/binding-darwin-arm64` under `optionalDependencies` — it declares `os: darwin, cpu: arm64`, so other platforms skip it rather than failing. Drop it if your CI resolves optionals correctly.

I didn't commit anything — this working directory is entirely untracked, so `git diff` is empty and the changes are on disk only.
